name: Entity Webhook
description: Configuration-driven inbound webhook ingestion: receives JSON POSTs at /webhook/{endpoint}/{source_type}, extracts values with JSONPath, transforms them with mutation plugins, and creates/updates (upserts) or deletes Drupal content entities via composite-key lookup, with pluggable request verification and queue-based async processing. Ships two optional submodules: Broadcast (outbound webhooks on entity CRUD, HMAC-signed, retried) and Polling (cron-scheduled external polling into the same pipeline).
project_description: Entity Webhook provides configuration-driven webhook ingestion and entity upsert for Drupal content entities, with no custom code required. External services POST JSON to a configurable endpoint (/webhook/{endpoint_name}/{source_type}); the module extracts values with JSONPath expressions, optionally transforms them with mutation plugins (timestamp formatting, string/regex replace, value mapping, price conversion, JSON encoding, array reshaping), and creates, updates, or deletes the target entity. Existing entities are matched by one or more identifier field mappings (composite-key lookup). Request verification is pluggable (HMAC signature, API key, IP/domain whitelist) and payloads are processed asynchronously through Drupal's queue during cron (with an optional synchronous mode per endpoint). A three-tier config-entity hierarchy models the setup: Webhook Endpoint (target entity type/bundle) -> Webhook Source Type (verification + operation) -> Webhook Field Mapping (resolver + mutation + identifier). Pre-save, post-save, and batch-complete events allow custom logic. Two optional submodules extend it: Entity Webhook Broadcast sends outbound webhooks when entities are created, updated, or deleted -- filtering with Drupal's Condition API, building payloads from entity fields, HMAC-signing requests, retrying with exponential backoff, and logging every delivery; Entity Webhook Polling pulls data from external APIs on a cron schedule (via dragonmantank/cron-expression), using SHA-256 change detection and feeding results into the same inbound pipeline. Maintained by Travis Tomka (droath).
